name: POST /api/leadflow/calendar/readiness - Refresh a rep's booking readiness
description: Re-reads one rep's calendar readiness from the scheduling service and records the MANUAL half of the checklist that no upstream can answer for us - working hours, PTO, buffers, minimum notice, daily maximum and timezone detection. 200 rather than 201: it refreshes an existing row per rep and creates nothing addressable. The GET on the same path reports the state and this one changes it; the pair is deliberate, because a screen that could only refresh would have to write before it could read. rep_user_id defaults to the CALLER when the body omits it, so a rep can refresh their own readiness without knowing their own id. Each check is stored separately because each fails for a different reason and is fixed by a different person, and may_receive_leads is the single verdict the routing engine consults - a rep failing any check must not be routed to, because a broken booking link turns a live enquiry into a dead one and nobody finds out. QA: depends on register and login for the bearer token.

testCases.name: Refresh a rep's readiness and set the manual flags
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all

errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, or present without a bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
rep_user_id is blank AND the session carries no user id
errorCases._whyNotReproducible: Unreachable through this route as authored: `authenticate` runs first, so any request reaching the handler carries a session user id and the body value falls back to it. Documented because the guard is real in the handler, not because a request can trigger it.
